questions: Which URL components may `api_base_url` contain, and exactly how are its path and authority combined with the declared operation path and `Host` header?
Are userinfo, query, fragment and multiple trailing slashes permitted in api_base_url, and exactly how is the declared path joined to such a URL?
May api_base_url contain user information, a query, a fragment, or a path prefix, and does removing a trailing slash remove one slash or all trailing slashes?

judgement.why: This asks the same api_base_url component, joining, authority, slash and Host-handling question on unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and exact URL joining and request-target rules
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

questions: Must authored inputs name exactly every input port and no others, and must `expected_outputs`, when present, name exactly every output port?
Must authored trial inputs, and expected outputs when present, contain exactly the declared port names, or are unexpected entries ignored or stored?

judgement.why: This asks the same authored trial-case port-coverage question on unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: Required and permitted trial-case input and expected-output port coverage
quotes: add_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown contract version; then RefusedError naming the first name in inputs that is not an input port of the contract version, then the first name in expected_outputs that is not an output port, each taken by name; then checks each input port and, when expected_outputs is given, each output port, in port name order, by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for value ports and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant for file ports, a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type; the first failing check, presence, carriage, schema then size, raises RefusedError naming port and check, and nothing is written. A trial case therefore names exactly the contract's input ports, and expected_outputs is either absent or names exactly every output port: a partial expected_outputs, and an empty object, is given and fails presence at its first missing port; only absence means no expected outputs.
precedent.why: The later notes require exactly every input port and, when expected_outputs is present, exactly every output port.

topics.topic: Exact host and resolved-address rules for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: What hosts satisfy the loopback exception, and must the address actually connected to be rechecked?
How must service_invoker decide that a host is loopback, especially for `localhost`, DNS names resolving to loopback, IPv4 alternative spellings and IPv6 addresses?

quotes:
17. **Request body and addresses.** A JSON request body is sent as its RFC 8785
    canonical bytes. "Loopback" (A09 rule 4) is an IP literal in
    `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`; no name is resolved to decide it.

send_prepared_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Sends the request exactly once to the URL host and port, never to the host header value; for https it verifies TLS with the URL host as the server name; it follows no redirect, ignores every proxy environment variable and retries nothing.
judgement.why: The later texts define loopback as an IPv4 127/8 or IPv6 ::1 literal, reject DNS-based classification, and require connection to the URL host and port rather than the Host header value.

topics.topic: How bindings reads and verifies service records at a specific manifest revision
questions: How does `bindings` obtain a service record at `manifest_revision`, and what failures mean that the revision or file is absent?
How must bindings read a service record at manifest_revision without changing the working tree, and what precisely proves that the bytes came from that revision?

judgement.why: This asks the same manifest-revision byte-selection question on unchanged texts.

precedent.topic: How a manifest revision selects and authenticates manifest bytes
quotes:
8. **The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
`<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
(A08 rules 1 and 6).
precedent.why: The later contract requires reading the manifest record as a Git object at the configured commit, never from the working tree.

precedent.topic: Startup manifest validation scope and ordering without an operation context
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: failure_detail values and precedence for sandbox, service, transport, and response failures
questions: For every timeout, resource, trap, crash, contract, transport and response-validation outcome, is `failure_detail` absent, a fixed code, or generated text, and when several defects exist which one supplies it?
What failure_detail is returned for DNS, connection, TLS, timeout, reset, EOF or malformed-response outcomes where no response body is available?

quotes: execute_function: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the wall deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the channel recorded any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the module failed to load, has no run, raised, or the process exited abnormally; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, a value output cannot be serialized to canonical JSON, a file output is not bytes, a many output is not a list, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value ceiling and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's: the module that stores or spools an output applies them after the execution has otherwise succeeded.

execute_function: [PROVENANCE] failure_detail holds only the type and message of an exception that escaped module loading or run, never anything the code printed, cut to at most the imported RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX constant bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary; it is None for succeeded and when no exception escaped.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed; when either cannot be confirmed the outputs are discarded and the result is outcome crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed of = models.DetailCode; the function returns that result and neither raises StopRequiredError nor stops the process, which its caller does after recording the execution, and it never retries.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.

send_prepared_request: [FIELD_PROJECTION] failure_detail is set only for an answer that is not used: when the body as read, reading stopping at the response ceiling, contains the bytes of the credential value sent with the request, exactly the text error body withheld: it contained the credential, searched before any cut; otherwise the body decoded as UTF-8 with each invalid sequence replaced by U+FFFD, cut at a character boundary to its longest prefix of at most the imported RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX constant UTF-8 bytes, never interpreted; the response status alone never means more than the outcome order says.
judgement.why: The later notes fix outcome precedence, restrict sandbox failure_detail to escaped exception type and message, assign cleanup_failed separately as a detail code, and define service failure_detail solely from an unused response body, with the credential-echo text taking precedence.
